newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Jan-Aug foreign investment approvals fall.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Jan-Aug foreign investment approvals fall.

text.p: Indonesia's Investment Minister Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo said on Monday January 1-August 31 foreign investment approvals were down to $22.2 billion compared to $29.7 billion in the same period last year.
He told reporters after meeting President Suharto that the falls were due to the absence of major projects.
"But in terms of total projects, there is an increase. During the January-August period, the total increased to 677 projects, compared to 508 projects in the same period last year," he added.
Sastrowardoyo said he believed foreign interest in investing in Indonesia remained high because of the rise in the total number of projects.
But he said he was not optimistic that foreign investment approvals in 1996 would match the 1995 figure.
Indonesia posted record foreign investment approvals last year amounting to $39.9 billion.
"We expect in the coming years, foreign investment will increase steadily following government regulations allowing tax holidays," he said.

But he gave no details on the proposed moves for granting tax holidays. Indonesia has said it will give tax breaks to newly-established companies in certain sectors but has not identified which industries will benefit.
